headline: Profit surges as APA beats production guidance, cuts debt
summary_short: APA's Q2 2026 net income rose 24% y/y to $747 million ($2.11 diluted EPS) as production and free cash flow of $738 million beat guidance; the company raised full-year U.S. oil production guidance, cut cost guidance, and lifted its 2026 cost-savings target.
summary_long: Revenue was $2.37B (+9.0% y/y, +2.0% q/q) while GAAP net income rose to $747M (+23.9% y/y, +67.5% q/q) on $2.11 diluted EPS; adjusted earnings were $669M ($1.89/share). Operating income of $1.28B was up 73.7% y/y. Reported production of 410,000 BOE/d and U.S. oil production of 123,500 b/d both topped guidance on drilling/completion efficiency gains in the Permian; Egypt was in-line. Free cash flow was $738M; APA repaid $673M of bond debt in the quarter, cutting net debt to $3.3B, and returned $189M via dividends and buybacks. APA raised full-year U.S. oil guidance to 123,000 b/d, cut LOE guidance by $25M to $1.5B, and raised its 2026 cost-savings target to $500M from $450M.

drivers.explanation: CEO cites strong operational execution across core assets, sustained top-tier performance, lower costs, lower capital intensity, and structural improvements over the past two years as a cost leader across the Permian and Egypt.

Total average realized oil price of $98.24/bbl (+50% y/y) more than offset a 10% y/y decline in total oil volumes and a much lower average natural gas price, per the release's own price and volume tables.
Cost-reduction initiatives lowered operating expenses and debt repayment cut annualized interest expense by more than $155 million, per the release; higher oil pricing also lifted revenue.
